Simulated soil profiles for examples and tests

Source: R/fixtures.R
edaphos_example_profiles.Rd

Returns synthetic soil profile data with the same shape as an ISRIC WoSIS extract (kind = "wosis_like") or a SoilData Dataverse bulk-density calibration set (kind = "soildata_like"). Every example, test and vignette in this package runs on these fixtures.

Usage

edaphos_example_profiles(
  kind = c("wosis_like", "soildata_like"),
  what = c("profiles", "horizons", "pedon", "all"),
  n = NULL
)

Arguments

kind

Which fixture: "wosis_like" (default) or "soildata_like".

what

Which element: "profiles" (default), "horizons", "pedon" (a single deep 9-horizon profile, wosis_like only), or "all" for the whole list including meta.

n

Optional row cap, applied after subsetting. NULL returns everything.

Value

A data frame with attr(, "synthetic") = TRUE, or the whole fixture list when what = "all".

Details

These are simulated values, not measurements. They are generated by data-raw/make_fixtures.R from published literature parameters – the Jackson et al. (1996) tropical-savanna root distribution (\(\beta = 0.972\)), a lognormal surface-SOC concentration with median 25 g/kg, and a round-numbered bulk-density pedotransfer form. Nothing in them is fitted to, or sampled from, any real dataset.

Coordinates are a regular lattice inside the Cerrado bounding box rather than a random scatter, so no fixture point can coincide with a survey site, and the synthetic origin is obvious on inspection.

The generator is seeded (set.seed(20260901L), recorded in the fixture's meta$seed), so both files are byte-reproducible by re-running the script.

What these fixtures cannot do: reproduce any published metric. Forty synthetic profiles do not yield the RMSE, coverage or effect-size figures quoted in the README and the manuscript. Those are reproducible only from a live fetch, via the scripts in data-raw/.

edaphos does not bundle or redistribute third-party soil data. Real profiles are the user's to obtain from the upstream services directly – ISRIC WoSIS, the SoilData Dataverse, USDA-NRCS – under those services' own licences, which vary per record.

References

Jackson RB, Canadell J, Ehleringer JR, Mooney HA, Sala OE, Schulze ED (1996). A global analysis of root distributions for terrestrial biomes. Oecologia 108:389-411.

Examples

prof <- edaphos_example_profiles()
str(prof[, c("profile_id", "soc_topsoil_gkg", "soilgrids_clay")])
#> 'data.frame':	120 obs. of  3 variables:
#>  $ profile_id     : chr  "SYN_001" "SYN_002" "SYN_003" "SYN_004" ...
#>  $ soc_topsoil_gkg: num  29.3 15.7 29.1 33 10 ...
#>  $ soilgrids_clay : num  22.8 51.5 23.7 62.2 51.2 18.3 19.3 17 46.4 52.1 ...

# Horizons of the first profile.
h <- edaphos_example_profiles(what = "horizons")
head(h[h$profile_id == prof$profile_id[1], ])
#>   profile_id   x   y top bottom soc_g_kg depth_mid bd_g_cm3 stock_mg_ha
#> 1    SYN_001 -58 -22   0     27    29.32      13.5       NA          NA
#> 2    SYN_001 -58 -22  27     65    12.50      46.0       NA          NA
#> 3    SYN_001 -58 -22  65     87     6.76      76.0       NA          NA
#> 4    SYN_001 -58 -22  87     98     5.17      92.5       NA          NA
#> 5    SYN_001 -58 -22  98    135     2.50     116.5       NA          NA

# Simulated, and it says so.
attr(prof, "synthetic")
#> [1] TRUE
